records.source: שַׁאֲל֨וּ מֵיְהוָ֤ה מָטָר֙ בְּעֵ֣ת מַלְק֔וֹשׁ יְהוָ֖ה עֹשֶׂ֣ה חֲזִיזִ֑ים וּמְטַר־גֶּ֨שֶׁם֙ יִתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם לְאִ֖ישׁ עֵ֥שֶׂב בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Ask from Yahweh rain in [the] time of [the] spring rain; Yahweh [is] making storm clouds, and showers of rain he gives to them, to each [one the] vegetation in the field.
pieces: Ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for rain in the season of the spring rain. \q It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who makes the storm clouds; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives them showers of rain \q and green plants in the field for everyone.

L.1: Ask rain from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the time of the spring rain; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is the one] making the storm clouds, \q and showers of rain {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives to them, \q to everyone the vegetation in the field.

R.1: Ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for rain in the spring. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who makes the storm clouds. \q He sends showers of rain \q and makes the plants in the fields grow for everyone.

decisions.choice: the spring rain: the last rains of the season, in March and April
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel rain falls only in the winter half of the year. The early rain of autumn softens the ground for plowing, and the late rain of spring swells the grain before harvest (Deuteronomy 11:14; Joel 2:23). Without the spring rain the harvest failed.

decisions.choice: ask rain from the LORD: the LORD, not the idols, gives the rain
decisions.reason: Many in Israel had looked to Baal, the storm god of Canaan, or to household gods and diviners, for rain and harvest (verse 2; Hosea 2:7-10; Jeremiah 14:22). The prophet calls the people to ask the LORD, who makes the storm clouds and gives the rain. It is a call back to trust in him.

decisions.choice: storm clouds: the thunderclouds that bring rain
decisions.reason: The word is used for the thunderbolt or the storm cloud that goes before the rain (Job 28:26; 38:25). The LORD makes the storm and sends the showers.

decisions.choice: It is the LORD who makes (B); green plants ... grow (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the LORD's name first for emphasis, which Balanced gives as "It is the LORD who" and Readable as "The LORD is the one who". Balanced and Readable say "green plants" for the field's vegetation.

records.heading: Ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for rain

records.source: כִּ֧י הַתְּרָפִ֣ים דִּבְּרוּ־אָ֗וֶן וְהַקּֽוֹסְמִים֙ חָ֣זוּ שֶׁ֔קֶר וַֽחֲלֹמוֹת֙ הַשָּׁ֣ואיְדַבֵּ֔רוּ הֶ֖בֶל יְנַֽחֵמ֑וּן עַל־כֵּן֙ נָסְע֣וּ כְמוֹ־צֹ֔אן יַעֲנ֖וּ כִּֽי־אֵ֥ין רֹעֶֽה׃פ
records.gloss: For the teraphim speak wickedness, and the diviners see falsehood, and dreams of worthlessness they speak, [with] futility they comfort; therefore they set out like sheep, they are afflicted, for there is no shepherd.
pieces: For the household gods speak deceit, and the diviners see lies; \q they tell dreams that are false \q and give comfort that is empty. \q So the people wander off like sheep; \q they suffer because they have no shepherd.

L.2: For the teraphim speak wickedness, and the diviners see falsehood; \q and they speak worthless dreams; \q they comfort in vain. \q Therefore they set out like sheep; \q they are afflicted, for there is no shepherd.

R.2: The household idols give answers that cannot be trusted, and the fortune-tellers see visions that are lies. \q They tell dreams that mean nothing. \q The comfort they give is useless. \q So the people wander like lost sheep. \q They suffer because they have no shepherd to lead them.

decisions.choice: the teraphim: household images used to seek guidance
decisions.reason: Teraphim were small images kept in the home (Genesis 31:19, 34) and used to ask for oracles (Ezekiel 21:26). They were condemned with other forms of divination (1 Samuel 15:23; 2 Kings 23:24). The meaning of the name is not known.

decisions.choice: the diviners see falsehood; dreams of worthlessness: the sources the people turned to for guidance are empty
decisions.reason: Diviners claimed to learn the future by signs and omens, a practice the law forbade (Deuteronomy 18:10-14). Dreams could come from God, but the prophets warned against those who told dreams of their own making (Jeremiah 23:25-32; 27:9). What these give is falsehood and "vapor", the word Ecclesiastes uses for what is fleeting and empty.

decisions.choice: like sheep with no shepherd: a people without true leaders
decisions.reason: A flock without a shepherd wanders and comes to harm. The picture is used of Israel without a king or a faithful leader (Numbers 27:17; 1 Kings 22:17; Ezekiel 34:5). In Matthew 9:36 and Mark 6:34 Jesus has compassion on the crowds because they are "like sheep without a shepherd".

decisions.choice: household gods (B); household idols (R); the people wander (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "teraphim"; Balanced and Readable say "household gods" and "household idols", as in Hosea 3:4. Balanced and Readable name "the people" as the ones who wander, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

records.source: עַל־הָֽרֹעִים֙ חָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֔י וְעַל־הָעַתּוּדִ֖ים אֶפְק֑וֹד כִּֽי־פָקַד֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֤וֹת אֶת־עֶדְרוֹ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה וְשָׂ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם כְּס֥וּס הוֹד֖וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Against the shepherds burns my anger, and on the male goats I will bring punishment; for Yahweh of hosts visits his flock, the house of Judah, and he will make them like his majestic horse in battle.
pieces: My anger blazes against the shepherds, \q and I will punish those who lead the flock; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies cares for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock, the house of Judah, \q and will make them like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} proud war horse in battle.

L.3: Against the shepherds {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger burns, \q and on the male goats I will visit [punishment]; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has visited {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock, the house of Judah, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set them like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majestic horse in battle.

R.3: I am angry with the shepherds who lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and I will punish those leaders. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies takes care of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock, the people of Judah. \q He will make them like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} proud horse in battle.

decisions.choice: the shepherds and the male goats: the leaders of the people
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East kings and rulers were called shepherds of their people (Jeremiah 23:1-4; Ezekiel 34:2-10). The male goats lead the flock, and the word is used for leaders and chiefs (Isaiah 14:9; Ezekiel 34:17). These are the leaders who let the people wander (verse 2). The text does not say who they were.

decisions.choice: I will punish ... the LORD has visited: one verb, two senses
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice. It means to look after someone, or to call someone to account. The LORD will call the leaders to account, and he has come to care for his flock. The play on the verb shows that his judgment on the leaders is his care for the people.

decisions.choice: like his majestic horse in battle: the weak flock becomes a war horse
decisions.reason: The sheep without a shepherd become the LORD's own war horse, splendid and fearless (Job 39:19-25). The LORD rides out to battle with his people (9:13-14).

decisions.choice: the male goats (L); the leaders of the flock (B); those leaders (R); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "male goats"; Balanced and Readable say what they stand for (m1). "The LORD of hosts" follows the wording set in Isaiah. Readable says "my people" for the flock the shepherds lead; the LORD is speaking, so "my" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} cares for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock

records.source: מִמֶּ֤נּוּ פִנָּה֙ מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יָתֵ֔ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֑ה מִמֶּ֛נּוּ יֵצֵ֥א כָל־נוֹגֵ֖שׂ יַחְדָּֽו׃
records.gloss: From him [the] corner, from him [the] peg, from him [the] bow of battle; from him will go out every ruler together.
pieces: From Judah will come the cornerstone, from Judah the tent peg, \q from Judah the battle bow; \q from Judah every ruler will come.

L.4: From him [will come the] cornerstone, from him [the] tent peg, \q from him [the] bow of battle; \q from him will go out every ruler together.

R.4: From the people of Judah will come a leader like a cornerstone, and one like a tent peg, \q and one like a bow used in battle. \q Every ruler will come from them.

decisions.choice: from him: from Judah
decisions.reason: "Him" refers back to the house of Judah in verse 3. The new leaders will come from God's people itself, in place of the shepherds who failed.

decisions.choice: the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow: leaders who hold the people together and fight for them
decisions.reason: Each picture stands for a leader. The cornerstone holds up a building (Psalm 118:22; Isaiah 28:16), and "the corners" of the people are its leaders (Judges 20:2; 1 Samuel 14:38). The tent peg holds a tent firm; Isaiah 22:23 calls Eliakim a peg driven into a firm place, on whom his family hangs. The battle bow is the leader in war.

decisions.choice: every ruler: every kind of leader
decisions.reason: The word usually means an oppressor or taskmaster, as in 9:8 and Exodus 3:7. Here it seems to mean a ruler in a good sense, one with power to command (Isaiah 60:17 uses it of rulers who bring peace). Some read it as the rulers who will oppress Judah's enemies.

decisions.choice: from Judah (B); From the people of Judah ... a leader like (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "Judah" for "him" (m1); Readable also says that the pictures are of leaders (m2).

records.source: וְהָי֨וּ כְגִבֹּרִ֜ים בּוֹסִ֨ים בְּטִ֤יט חוּצוֹת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנִ֨לְחֲמ֔וּ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּ֑ם וְהֹבִ֖ישׁוּ רֹכְבֵ֥י סוּסִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they will be like warriors trampling in [the] mud of [the] streets in battle, and they will fight, for Yahweh [is] with them, and they will put to shame riders of horses.
pieces: They will be like warriors in battle, trampling the enemy into the mud of the streets. \q They will fight, \q since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with them, \q and the horsemen will be put to shame.

L.5: And they will be like warriors trampling in the mud of [the] streets in battle; \q and they will fight, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with them, \q and they will put to shame [the] riders on horses.

R.5: They will be like soldiers in battle who trample their enemies into the mud of the streets. \q They will fight, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with them. \q They will defeat the enemy's horsemen.

decisions.choice: trampling in the mud of the streets: treading down their enemies like mud
decisions.reason: Conquered enemies are pictured as mud trodden down in the streets (2 Samuel 22:43; Micah 7:10). The warriors of Judah trample their foes as easily as they walk through the mud.

decisions.choice: they will fight, for the LORD is with them: the victory is his
decisions.reason: Judah's people fight, but they win because the LORD is with them, as he was with Israel in its battles of old (Joshua 1:5; Judges 6:16).

decisions.choice: the riders on horses: the enemy's cavalry
decisions.reason: Horses and chariots were the strength of great armies, and Judah had little of either (9:10). The foot soldiers of Judah will put the enemy's horsemen to shame, the reverse of what anyone would expect (Psalm 20:8).

decisions.choice: trampling the enemy into the mud (B); their enemies; the enemy's horsemen (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the object of "trampling" (m1). Readable says "defeat" for "put to shame" and names the horsemen as the enemy's (m3).

records.source: וְגִבַּרְתִּ֣י׀אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֤ית יוֹסֵף֙ אוֹשִׁ֔יעַ וְהֽוֹשְׁבוֹתִים֙ כִּ֣י רִֽחַמְתִּ֔ים וְהָי֖וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־זְנַחְתִּ֑ים כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וְאֶעֱנֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will strengthen [the] house of Judah, and [the] house of Joseph I will save; and I will bring them back, for I have compassion on them, and they will be as [if] I had not rejected them; for I [am] Yahweh their God, and I will answer them.
pieces: I will make the house of Judah strong and save the house of Joseph. \q I will bring them back, because I have compassion on them, \q and it will be as if I had never cast them off. \q I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and I will answer them.

L.6: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and the house of Joseph I will save; \q and I will bring them back, for I have had compassion on them, \q and they will be as [if] I had not spurned them; \q because I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and I will answer them.

R.6: I will make the people of Judah strong, and I will rescue the northern tribes of Israel. \q I will bring them home, because I feel deep love for them. \q It will be as if I had never turned them away. \q I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and I will answer when they call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the house of Joseph: the northern tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Joseph was the father of Ephraim and Manasseh, the largest of the northern tribes. "The house of Joseph" stands for the northern kingdom, also called Ephraim (verse 7), whose people had been carried off by Assyria. Judah and Joseph together are the whole people (Ezekiel 37:16-19).

decisions.choice: I will bring them back: one of two readings combined in the written form
alternatives: I will settle them (in their land)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew form looks like a blend of two verbs: "I will bring them back" and "I will make them dwell". The reading tradition and most ancient translations take the first, which is followed here, as in verse 10. The second would mean "I will settle them" in their land. Either way the LORD restores his people.

decisions.choice: I have compassion on them ... as though I had not rejected them: a full restoring
decisions.reason: The verb for compassion is the tender love of a parent (Psalm 103:13); it is the word in the name of Hosea's daughter Lo-ruhamah (Hosea 1:6; 2:25). The LORD will take his people back as if he had never cast them off.

decisions.choice: I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them: the covenant bond renewed
decisions.reason: "I am the LORD their God" is the language of the covenant (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:44-45). To "answer" is to hear prayer and act on it (13:9; Isaiah 58:9).

decisions.choice: the northern tribes of Israel; I feel deep love for them; I will answer when they call to me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the house of Joseph" (m1) and "answer" (m4). The LORD is speaking of himself, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

records.source: וְהָי֤וּ כְגִבּוֹר֙ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְשָׂמַ֥ח לִבָּ֖ם כְּמוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּבְנֵיהֶם֙ יִרְא֣וּ וְשָׂמֵ֔חוּ יָגֵ֥ל לִבָּ֖ם בַּיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will be like a warrior Ephraim, and will rejoice their heart as [with] wine; and their children will see and rejoice; will rejoice their heart in Yahweh.
pieces: The people of Ephraim will be like warriors, \q and their hearts will be glad as if with wine. \q Their children will see it and be glad; \q their hearts will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.7: And Ephraim will be like a warrior, \q and their heart will be glad as [with] wine; \q and their children will see [it] and be glad; \q their heart will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: The people of Ephraim will be like strong soldiers. \q They will be as happy as people who have drunk wine. \q Their children will see it and be glad. \q Their hearts will be full of joy in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Ephraim: the northern tribes, as the house of Joseph in verse 6
decisions.reason: Ephraim was the leading tribe of the north, and its name stands for the northern kingdom, as often in Hosea. The scattered northern tribes are to share in the victory and joy of Judah.

decisions.choice: their heart will be glad as with wine: a great and open joy
decisions.reason: Wine "gladdens the heart" (Psalm 104:15). The joy of the restored people is like the joy of a feast, and it passes to their children, who see what the LORD has done.

decisions.choice: The people of Ephraim (B, R); their hearts (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of Ephraim as one warrior with one heart. Balanced and Readable say "the people of Ephraim" and use plurals, as English does for a people.

records.source: אֶשְׁרְקָ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם וַאֲקַבְּצֵ֖ם כִּ֣י פְדִיתִ֑ים וְרָב֖וּ כְּמ֥וֹ רָבֽוּ׃
records.gloss: I will whistle for them and I will gather them, for I have redeemed them; and they will be many as they were many.
pieces: I will whistle for them and gather them in, because I have set them free, \q and they will be as many as they were before.

L.8: I will whistle for them and I will gather them in, for I have redeemed them; \q and they will become as many as they were before.

R.8: I will whistle to call them together and gather them, because I have rescued them. \q There will be as many of them as there were before.

decisions.choice: I will whistle for them: the signal that calls them together
decisions.reason: A shepherd or beekeeper whistled to call his flock or his bees (Judges 5:16). Isaiah 5:26 and 7:18 use the same verb of the LORD whistling for the nations to come against his people. Now he whistles to bring his own people home.

decisions.choice: I have redeemed them: set them free, as from slavery
decisions.reason: The verb means to ransom or set free by paying a price, and it is used for the LORD's freeing of Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8; 13:6). Here the freeing has been decided already, though the gathering is still to come.

decisions.choice: as many as they were before: as they grew in Egypt
decisions.reason: The people will grow again to their former numbers. The words recall how Israel multiplied in Egypt (Exodus 1:7, 12) and the promise to Abraham of descendants beyond counting (Genesis 22:17).

decisions.choice: before (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they will be many as they were many". Every level says "as many as they were before", and Literal leaves the word unbracketed because it only puts the repeated verb into English.

records.source: וְאֶזְרָעֵם֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים וּבַמֶּרְחַקִּ֖ים יִזְכְּר֑וּנִי וְחָי֥וּ אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם וָשָֽׁבוּ׃
records.gloss: And I will sow them among [the] peoples, and in far places they will remember me; and they will live with their children and return.
pieces: Though I scatter them among the peoples like seed, \q in faraway lands they will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q they and their children will live, and they will come back.

L.9: Though I sow them among [the] peoples, \q yet in far places they will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and they will live with their children and return.

R.9: I will scatter them among the nations like seed, \q but even in faraway lands they will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They and their children will stay alive, and they will come home.

decisions.choice: sow them among the peoples: scatter them, as seed that will grow
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for sowing seed. The LORD's scattering of his people among the nations is pictured as sowing, which looks forward to a harvest; Hosea 2:25 uses the same verb of the LORD sowing his people in the land. The scattering is not the end of them.

decisions.choice: though I sow them ... yet they will remember me: the scattering and the remembering together
alternatives: I scattered them among the peoples, but ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two clauses with "and". The sense is that even when they are scattered far away, they will remember the LORD and turn back to him (Deuteronomy 30:1-3; 1 Kings 8:47-48). The verb may be read of a scattering still to come or of the one that had already happened; it is read here as the first.

decisions.choice: scatter them ... like seed (B, R); come back, come home (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "scatter ... like seed" to keep both the scattering and the picture of sowing (m1).

records.source: וַהֲשִֽׁיבוֹתִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמֵֽאַשּׁ֖וּר אֲקַבְּצֵ֑ם וְאֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ גִּלְעָ֤ד וּלְבָנוֹן֙ אֲבִיאֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will bring them back from [the] land of Egypt, and from Assyria I will gather them, and to [the] land of Gilead and Lebanon I will bring them, and [room] will not be found for them.
pieces: I will bring them home from the land of Egypt \q and gather them from Assyria. \q I will bring them to the land of Gilead and to Lebanon, \q until there is no room left for them.

L.10: And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt, \q and from Assyria I will gather them; \q and to the land of Gilead and Lebanon I will bring them, \q and [room] will not be found for them.

R.10: I will bring them home from Egypt \q and gather them out of Assyria. \q I will lead them into the lands of Gilead and Lebanon, \q and there will not be enough room for them all.

decisions.choice: Egypt and Assyria: the lands of Israel's oppression and exile
decisions.reason: Egypt was the land of Israel's slavery, and Assyria the empire that carried off the northern tribes. By Zechariah's day Assyria had fallen long before, and the names stand for the lands to the south and to the north-east where Israel's people were scattered (Isaiah 11:11; 27:13; Hosea 11:11).

decisions.choice: Gilead and Lebanon: the lands east of the Jordan and in the north
decisions.reason: Gilead was the land east of the Jordan, rich in pasture, held by Israel's tribes from the time of Moses (Numbers 32). Lebanon was the mountain land in the far north. Together they mark the full extent of the old land of Israel, given back to its people (Micah 7:14; Jeremiah 50:19).

decisions.choice: room will not be found for them: there will be too many people for the land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "it will not be found for them". The sense is that the land will be too small for the returning people, as Isaiah 49:19-20 promises.

decisions.choice: no room left (B); not enough room for them all (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "room", which Literal brackets (m3).

records.source: וְעָבַ֨ר בַּיָּ֜ם צָרָ֗ה וְהִכָּ֤ה בַיָּם֙ גַּלִּ֔ים וְהֹבִ֕ישׁוּ כֹּ֖ל מְצוּל֣וֹת יְאֹ֑ר וְהוּרַד֙ גְּא֣וֹן אַשּׁ֔וּר וְשֵׁ֥בֶט מִצְרַ֖יִם יָסֽוּר׃
records.gloss: And he will pass through [the] sea of distress, and he will strike in [the] sea [the] waves, and will dry up all [the] depths of [the] Nile; and will be brought down [the] pride of Assyria, and [the] scepter of Egypt will depart.
pieces: He will cross the sea of distress \q and strike down its waves, \q and the Nile will dry up to its depths. \q Assyria's pride will be brought low, \q and Egypt's scepter will pass away.

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will cross the sea of distress \q and strike [the] waves in the sea, \q and all the Nile's depths will dry up; \q and Assyria's pride will be brought down, \q and Egypt's scepter will depart.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will go through the sea of trouble \q and strike its waves, \q and the deepest parts of the Nile River will dry up. \q Proud Assyria will be brought down, \q and Egypt will no longer rule.

decisions.choice: he will pass through the sea and strike the waves: a new crossing of the sea, as at the exodus
decisions.reason: The LORD once divided the sea and dried it up for his people to cross from Egypt (Exodus 14:21-22; Psalm 106:9). The return from exile is pictured as a new exodus, with the LORD going ahead of his people and drying up the waters, as in Isaiah 11:15-16 and 51:10.

decisions.choice: he will pass through: the LORD goes before his people
alternatives: the people will pass through the sea of distress
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. It is read here of the LORD, who strikes the waves and dries up the Nile; the next verse speaks of him again. It may instead refer to the people, spoken of as one, crossing the sea of distress; the Septuagint reads "they will pass through".

decisions.choice: the sea of distress: the sea as a picture of trouble
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "sea, distress". It is read as "the sea of distress", that is, the sea of trouble the people must cross. A small change in the letters would give "the sea of Egypt", as in Isaiah 11:15.

decisions.choice: the Nile; the pride of Assyria; the scepter of Egypt: the great powers brought low
decisions.reason: The Nile was the life of Egypt; to dry it up is to strike at Egypt's heart (Isaiah 19:5-7). The scepter is the rod of a king's rule. The powers that once ruled over Israel will lose their hold.

decisions.choice: The LORD will go through (R); Proud Assyria; Egypt will no longer rule (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one who acts (m2) and says what the pride and the scepter stand for (m4). Balanced begins its sentence with "He", where the deity_pronoun setting is not needed.

records.source: וְגִבַּרְתִּים֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּבִשְׁמ֖וֹ יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will strengthen them in Yahweh, and in his name they will walk, declaration of Yahweh.
pieces: I will give them strength in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and they will walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And I will make them strong in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name they will walk about, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: I will make them strong through {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q They will live as people who bear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I will strengthen them in the LORD: the LORD speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: The LORD is speaking, yet he says "in the LORD" and "his name". The prophets sometimes have God speak of himself in the third person in this way (Hosea 1:7; Genesis 19:24). The strength the people will have is the LORD's own.

decisions.choice: walk in his name: live under his authority and in loyalty to him
decisions.reason: To "walk" is to live one's life. To walk in the name of the LORD is to live as his people, trusting in him and obeying him (Micah 4:5). The Septuagint has "they will boast in his name".

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (L, B); says the LORD (R); live as people who bear his name (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set in Isaiah. Readable explains "walk in his name" (m2).
